prompt_en: Photograph a woman wearing visible spring fashion layers, using the supplied photograph as the face and short black bob reference. She is fastening a fresh botanical print to a drying line inside a small riverside print workshop just after a spring shower. A newly opened sash window has sent a breath of air through the room: the bottom of the pale paper curls toward her while a gauze curtain lifts behind the taut line. At the shutter, her right thumb and index finger squeeze a small metal spring clip around the print's dry upper margin and the line; her left thumb and fingertips steady its dry lower corner beside her right hip. Her shoulders turn slightly toward the paper, both elbows bend naturally, and her weight rests on two feet set a little apart. The lower corner has stopped fluttering in her hand while the free opposite corner still bends in the breeze. Her eyes follow the upper clip; her mouth holds the beginning of a relieved smile, with the softness and natural asymmetry of the reference face intact. The held print is beside her torso, leaving the front clothing layers legible. Her ivory sleeveless knitted vest has repeated open diamond holes made by visible intersecting yarn loops, bounded by dense ribbing around the neckline and hem. These open stitches belong to her outer ivory vest. Open stitches of the knit garment leave clear gaps bounded by connected yarn paths. The opaque yarn and the surface visible through each true gap remain distinct. Beneath the holes sits a pale muted peach sheer long-sleeved blouse, with a sage opaque camisole forming a clear straight upper edge under the transparent chest panel. Above that camisole edge the sheer blouse transmits the skin tone; below it the same sheer fabric transmits the sage surface. Across the arms the peach translucent sleeves reveal softened skin through their fabric, and the gathered cuffs form small folds at each wrist. The peach blouse is a translucent organza layer, with visible weave seam and edge along its cuff and hem. Window light passes through the fabric from behind her sleeves. The sage opaque underlayer remains partly visible through the blouse, and folds become denser and less transparent where the sleeves gather into the cuffs. The knitted vest sits outside the blouse, its yarn remaining opaque while its true gaps reveal the separate fabric beneath. A strip of the blouse extends below the vest's ribbed hem and lies over the upper edge of a warm mushroom-taupe pleated midi skirt. Her blouse and skirt share a quiet peach-and-mushroom warmth, making two soft adjoining tones against the cooler sage inner top; their different lightness keeps the blouse hem separate from the skirt waistband. The skirt's broad folds fall vertically, with a distinct diagonal wrap edge crossing its front. A second clipped sheet hangs farther along the line, and a low workbench carries an ink-stained cloth and an open wooden type tray; their small irregularities suggest a working room rather than a showroom. Frame her from head to mid-calf in a vertical photograph, slightly to the right of center, with the botanical sheet occupying the space beside her and the workshop window giving a shallow view of the river. Soft window light from behind her right shoulder grazes the yarn loops, preserves the peach fabric's transmission and the camisole's solid coverage, and leaves a quiet shadow between the overlapping hems. Use a natural perspective and enough depth of field to read her face, finger contacts, knit openings and the three clothing layers together. The photograph should feel like a delicate, practical interruption caught at the instant she regains control, with her understated warmth carrying a subtle attraction through attention and bearing.
